leads.work: Moving terminated counterparties' deals into the bankruptcy books. Risk/credit staff (Richardson, Balfour-Flanagan, Anderson) send spreadsheet lists every day, often several a day, Risk staff (Love, Giron) forward them, and IT (Cecilia Cheung) runs scripts to move and retranslate the deals. A chain of reconciliation questions follows each round.
leads.why: It recurs every day: 'many more deals listed to move on Tuesday', 'stragglers', 'daily updates from legal'. The volume is large: more than 10,000 deals to retranslate, 2,923 deals in one move, and 'with 7,000 lines... at least a day for risk to move manually'. Lists are combined by hand into a master cumulative spreadsheet, the same items are re-checked ('These deals have been moved previously'), and moves are sometimes reversed (MIDLANDCOGEN). Every request triggers the same clarifying questions about book ID, commodity code, cutoff date and financial only.

leads.work: Master Termination Log and daily termination list from Legal, sent to about 80 people and then forwarded again down the chain.
leads.why: Legal compiles it every day and sends it out to a long list, and each group then re-forwards it. It feeds the bankruptcy book moves above.

leads.work: Manual billing adjustments for Transwestern capacity releases with a 50/50 sharing of the marketing fee (the ENA/Burlington release). The rate arithmetic is worked out by hand in email each month, and a manual invoice adjustment and a revenue booking follow.
leads.why: The January and February calculations were done separately using 'your format for January', so this repeats monthly. The invoice needs a manual adjustment, and staff are unsure which accounting account to use.

leads.work: Transwestern Capacity Release Report, an XLS sent to about 20 people and re-issued whenever a release changes.
leads.why: The report is a recurring distribution with revised versions ('will send an updated file if necessary').

leads.work: Weekly California Capacity Report: Transwestern and El Paso deliveries, utilization percentages and Gas Daily prices, typed into an email each week.
leads.why: It has the same format every week, with the numbers pulled from pipeline data and Gas Daily, so it could be generated automatically.

leads.work: Emailing customers one by one about a Transwestern available-capacity posting and bid deadline.
leads.why: Several near-identical 'Due today at 5:00...hope you guys bid!' emails went out the same morning. A distribution list or automatic notice from the EBB (TW's electronic bulletin board) would replace them.

leads.work: Mojave interconnect imbalance reconciliation with El Paso: spreadsheets of measured versus scheduled volumes sent by hand.
leads.why: This is ongoing operational balance agreement (OBA) reconciliation work done through spreadsheets.

leads.work: El Paso Electric (EPE) preschedule spreadsheet and daily model, kept by hand in Excel and emailed every day. Errors keep turning up: missing tags, wrong megawatt figures, a cancelled tag still shown. Staff discussed moving the task to the real-time desk.
leads.why: The schedules were wrong 'for yet another day' and were caught only because dispatchers flagged them. Staff noted this is 'the only income we have currently for real-time' and is a relationship risk. Paper filing of the daily printouts is also required.

leads.work: El Paso data scrape and creation of the ISO (California grid operator) day-ahead and hour-ahead finals. The scrape is fragile: Netscape dependency, server moves, frequent URL changes, H: drive mapping errors.
leads.why: Repeated outages stopped the finals from being created, and new URLs were emailed several times. Each failure costs night-shift time.

leads.work: Forwarding the daily Energy Market Report and the Gas Daily/Power Daily PDFs by hand to trader lists, plus requests to add people to the distribution.
leads.why: An assistant re-forwards the reports every day, and keeping the distribution list current needs back-and-forth emails.

leads.work: Approving small expense reports one at a time in Concur.
leads.why: Approval emails arrive one by one for small amounts ($57 to $91) from the same group.

leads.work: Netco/UBS systems access and migration: collecting user lists by email (Sitara access, Stack Manager survey, trader lists), renaming desks and books, and changing references from EOL to OLT/ETX.
leads.why: Several requests and reminders were needed to gather access lists ('still need a list', 'still waiting on a response'). The setup was a 'mass set up' followed by eRequest.

leads.work: Maintaining P&L, hedgestrip and curve spreadsheets with macros, links and hard-coded book names that break whenever books or environments change.
leads.why: Macros, OA tabs and Weapon-X links had to be edited by hand, and the Refresh Booklist button pressed. Curve files needed manual environment edits. Each region uses a different P&L format, and there is a suggestion to standardize and to use a macro instead of links.

leads.work: Integration testing and daily status reporting for the Netco/UBS cutover, with status files due at 3:00 every day.
leads.why: Heavy recurring coordination involving about 80 people on the distribution, with scripted end-to-end tests repeated across systems.

leads.work: Valuing deals for specific counterparties by hand (Peoples cash flow, NSS) and restating P&L after booking errors.
leads.why: Values were questioned ('way too high') and requested again at a different date. Kills and annuities were booked wrongly, so January P&L had to be restated.

leads.work: Extracting files of active financial deals and positions for the credit group and reconciling counterparty exposure between Risk and Credit Aggregation.
leads.why: Files are produced every day and saved to the dropbox because they are too big to email, extra filters are requested, and a reconciliation of matching Post IDs is needed.

leads.work: HR onboarding paperwork chased by mass email: UBS forms, drug-test reminders, and repeated orientation sessions.
leads.why: Several urgent reminders with deadlines went to more than 170 people, and incomplete applications had to be completed in person. Payroll depended on paper forms.

leads.work: Collecting time reports and tracking shift-schedule trades by email.
leads.why: A recurring 'Time Reports Due Today' reminder, and shift trades have to be both emailed and written on the paper schedule.

leads.work: The Capacity Analysis System (CAS) is slow to deliver fixes, which delays the hand-off from Facility Planning to Marketing.
leads.why: There is an explicit complaint that the system 'is not responding to our expectations', and a meeting was called.

leads.work: Rodeo ticket requests and allocation collected by email with ranked choices.
leads.why: A manual allocation process handled through email.

leads.work: An unexplained $19,937 vendor check sent to MPC, which needs investigation.
leads.why: This looks like a payment-control or reconciliation problem.
